text: A gitignored path is outside the ingest corpus: it produces no residue, blocks no read, and a project containing one ingests exactly as if it were absent (D29) -- while an untracked-but-not-ignored artefact is still ingested, and a project with no git degrades to everything-in-scope. Each residue path is reported once. **The corpus is a function of the repository, never of the machine**: the ignore sources are the ignore files committed in the tree, and NOT `core.excludesFile`. Reopened WP-03 after close: found at WP-06 measuring `intent search`, whose 24 residue lines were 100% `.DS_Store` and 100% gitignored, which makes every macOS checkout unreadable and every macOS migration BLOCKED at AC-10.2. **Machine-scope defect measured at `2e490e5`, which is why this stays unsatisfied**: identical bytes in `intent/probe_global.sql` and `intent/probe_local.dat` yield a residue line for the second and silence for the first, because `~/.gitignore_global:20` carries `*.sql`. **Correction to my own second claim, from cc**: I reported the asymmetry also holding "in a project with no `.git` at all", and it does not -- a standalone directory outside any repository returns an empty ignore set exactly as this AC requires. My fixture had no `.git` **of its own** but sat inside one (`/Users/matts/.claude` is a repository, and the scratch directory is under it), and git resolves a repo at-or-above, correctly. So the AC's no-git wording was right and only the implementation was wrong -- the defect is the machine-scope one above, and my supporting claim overstated its reach in the direction that made it look worse. D29 derives the rule from "a path git can never commit can never be canon", and a path excluded only by one developer's global excludes is freely committable by anyone else, so it was never in that class. Two developers at one commit ingest different corpora, invisibly, and AC-10.2 makes that difference decide a migration BLOCK -- a fleet member can migrate cleanly on one machine and block on another. This repository already collides with the pattern: it commits `schema/ddl.sql` and carries a `!` exception solely to defeat the global `*.sql`. The `.git/info/exclude` sub-choice is **closed as DROP** (cc's call, ratified by vc 2026-08-15 on the same derivation): it is per-clone and uncommitted, so a fresh clone of one commit would disagree about what the project contains, and a path excluded there is one `git add` from being committed by anyone who has not written it -- never in D29's "can NEVER be committed" class. **Fixed at `3ebaf55` and verified independently at `fc6bbc6`** on three identical-byte probes in a purpose-built repository: the committed-`.gitignore` probe is excluded, the global-only probe is now IN scope, the unmatched probe is in scope, and Intent correctly disagrees with `git check-ignore` on exactly the global-only file. The no-git arm re-measured outside any repository -- `.DS_Store`, `.sql` and unmatched all in scope, degrading to everything-in-scope as the AC requires
